title: 5-Minute Quickstart Guide
summary: Add Kromium to your Gradle project, bootstrap the Chromium engine, and create your first browser instance.

sections.title: Prerequisites
sections.content:
Before integrating Kromium, ensure your environment meets the minimum runtime requirements:
- **JDK:** Java 17 or higher (Java 21 LTS recommended, e.g., Eclipse Temurin).
- **Supported Operating Systems:**
  - **Windows:** 10 / 11 (x86_64, ARM64)
  - **macOS:** 12+ Monterey, Ventura, Sonoma, Sequoia (Intel x86_64, Apple Silicon ARM64)
  - **Linux:** Ubuntu 20.04+, Debian 11+, Fedora, Arch (x86_64, ARM64) with GTK 3+ installed.

sections.title: Adding Gradle Dependencies
sections.content: Add Kromium to your build.gradle.kts using either Gradle Version Catalog or direct coordinates.

sections.title: Basic Engine Lifecycle & First Browser
sections.content:
Kromium separates the engine lifecycle into three clean stages:
1. **KromiumEngine**: Manages the underlying native Chromium runtime, process models, and shared cache.
2. **KromiumClient**: Represents an isolated session (cookies, storage, and global listeners).
3. **KromiumBrowser**: Represents a single web page view and its control facades.

sections.title: Controlling the Browser
sections.content: Once created, browser exposes dedicated facades for all web operations: navigation, DevTools, downloads, cookies, and automation.

sections.title: Observing Reactive Navigation State
sections.content: browser.navigation.navigationState is a coroutine StateFlow<KromiumNavigationState> that continuously emits real-time loading updates.
